|===

What each backend states on constant time, as the capability table read it:

* `hash2`: Boost.Hash2 1.92: its headers (boost/hash2/) state no constant-time property.
* `webcrypto`: The Web Cryptography API (W3C Recommendation, 2017) states no constant-time property of digest, sign or deriveBits; each JavaScript runtime's implementation decides, and webcpp reads none.

The default of `macs::hmac<digests::md5>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha1>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_224>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_256>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_384>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_512>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_512_224>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha2_512_256>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha3_224>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha3_256>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha3_384>`, `macs::hmac<digests::sha3_512>`, `macs::hmac<digests::ripemd_160>`, `macs::hmac<digests::blake2b>` and `macs::hmac<digests::blake2s_256>`: `hash2` on every target, whatever the program links (<<hash-default-backend>>).

`webcrypto` serves the asynchronous family alone, on Emscripten, where the type of its asynchronous call names it (<<hash-async-webcrypto>>).
